extracted.intended_audience: state air quality agencies (Guam), regulated entities in the Piti-Cabras area, environmental stakeholders, and environmental attorneys/advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule establishing a Clean Data Determination (CDD) for the Piti-Cabras, Guam SO2 nonattainment area under the Clean Air Act, describing legal effects, suspended and unsuspended requirements, basis for the determination, and procedural/legal review details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean Data Determination (CDD) concept and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: When air quality data demonstrate that a nonattainment area has attained the relevant NAAQS, the EPA may issue a Clean Data Determination (CDD) that the area is attaining the NAAQS; a final CDD suspends the obligation to submit certain attainment planning requirements for as long as the area continues to attain the NAAQS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CDD suspends CAA requirements that are specifically designed to help an area achieve attainment while the area continues to meet the NAAQS. A CDD does not constitute redesignation to attainment under section 107(d)(3) of the CAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspended attainment planning requirements (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: A final CDD suspends the obligation to submit: an attainment demonstration; reasonably available control measures, including reasonably available control technology (RACM/RACT); a reasonable further progress (RFP) demonstration; emissions limitations and control measures as necessary to provide for attainment; and contingency measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific elements of a CAA part D nonattainment area SIP are suspended for as long as the area continues to attain the relevant NAAQS. The final rule repeats that list when describing the scope of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-suspended CAA 172(c) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The remaining CAA 172(c) requirements — namely, the base year emissions inventory and nonattainment new source review (NNSR) requirements — are not suspended by a CDD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after issuance of a CDD, the State remains obligated to submit the base year emissions inventory and to show the area is covered by an EPA-approved NNSR program; these obligations persist despite the suspension of other planning elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for CDD: air quality data and modeling demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA may base a CDD on air quality data demonstrating attainment; in this action, the EPA determined the Piti-Cabras area has attained the 2010 1-hour SO2 NAAQS based on air dispersion modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence showing attainment (monitoring data or modeling) is the factual basis for a CDD. The final rule explicitly states the determination is 'based on air dispersion modeling' for the Piti-Cabras area.

rubrics_metrics.name: CDD does not equal redesignation; redesignation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuance of a final CDD does not constitute redesignation of the area to attainment under CAA section 107(d)(3). Redesignation requires (1) a formal request by the state, (2) EPA determination that the area meets the CAA requirements for redesignation, and (3) EPA approval of a state-submitted maintenance plan that ensures continued attainment for the successive 10-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule emphasizes the procedural and substantive distinctions between a CDD (suspension of certain requirements while attainment continues) and a redesignation (permanent change in designation contingent on state submission and EPA approval of required elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: State obligations post-CDD
rubrics_metrics.description: Following issuance of a CDD, the State remains obligated to submit nonattainment planning requirements that are not suspended (e.g., base year emissions inventory) and to demonstrate the area is covered by an EPA-approved NNSR program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule notes the EPA had previously found the base year emissions inventory complete and proposed approval of Guam's NNSR program; nonetheless, the State's obligations to submit required elements remain in force where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of EPA FIP obligation and sanctions clocks
rubrics_metrics.description: A final CDD suspends the EPA's obligation to promulgate a Federal Implementation Plan (FIP) and suspends the sanctions clocks associated with a finding of failure to submit, for the elements suspended by the CDD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule cites a prior finding (Nov 3, 2020) and explains that issuance of the CDD satisfies certain consent-decree obligations and suspends related FIP and sanctions timing so long as the area continues to attain the NAAQS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation requirement and comment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed action provided a 30-day public comment period; the EPA received one comment unrelated to the action and no comments that changed the assessment, so the EPA finalized the CDD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule documents the public comment period length and summarizes that no adverse comments were received; where no adverse comments are received, EPA may finalize the action consistent with administrative procedure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and codification
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule is effective October 20, 2025, and the CDD is codified at 40 CFR 52.2679(c), which adds the determination that the specified portion of Guam has attained the 2010 1-hour SO2 NAAQS and describes the suspended requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulatory text includes the precise codified language and the geographic description in CFR; effective date establishes when the suspension of obligations and other legal effects begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review timeline and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 307(b)(1), petitions for judicial review of this action must be filed in the appropriate U.S. Court of Appeals by November 17, 2025. Filing a petition for reconsideration does not affect the finality of the rule for purposes of judicial review or extend the time for filing, and the action may not be challenged later in proceedings to enforce its requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule provides the statutory deadline and warns that later litigation avenues are limited; parties should file timely petitions in the appropriate circuit to seek review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and Executive Order review determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA's determinations under various statutes and Executive Orders: this action is not a 'significant regulatory action' under Executive Order 12866 and Executive Order 14192; it does not impose PRA information collection burdens; the Regulatory Flexibility Act analysis finds no significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; it contains no unfunded mandates under UMRA; it has no federalism or Tribal implications; EO 13045 and EO 13211 do not apply; NTTAA section 12(d) is not applicable; the action is subject to the Congressional Review Act and is not a 'major rule'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These determinations summarize applicability (or lack thereof) of cross-cutting procedural and economic statutes and Executive Orders to the rule. They serve as criteria for evaluating regulatory impacts and inter-agency review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic description and applicability of the nonattainment area
rubrics_metrics.description: The Piti-Cabras nonattainment area is defined as 'the portion of Guam within a 6.074-km radius centered on UTM Easting 249,601.60 m, and UTM Northing 1,489,602.00 m (UTM Zone 55N),' which delineates the geographic scope of the CDD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise geographic delineation in the rule determines which areas and sources are covered by the suspended requirements and which entities are directly affected by the CDD.
